subject: Deployment mode selection & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Subject: Re: Intro + Demo — deployment follow-up

Hi Samir / Leah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary: Lumina is evaluating options for migrating model inference away from your current self-hosted GPU cluster toward a managed solution. Primary constraints you mentioned: PHI/data residency, 99th percentile latency targets around 150ms for chat flows, and predictable monthly spend for the analytics team.

- Deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fastest time-to-value), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), and Private (VPC/on-prem for compliance).

- Recommended immediate next steps:
  1) Share migration checklist (attached) and initial SLA for Dedicated (attached).
  2) Tech deep-dive with our SE to map your Triton/self-hosted setup to Redwood capacity sizing (I’ll loop Dev in).
  3) If PHI is required, start Private/VPC conversation — it’s the longer path (4–8 weeks onboarding typical).

Could you confirm the following so we can scope:
- Current average and peak QPS for inference?
- Typical model sequence length (tokens) and concurrency profile?
- Any contractual/regulatory requirements for data residency or KMS?

I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical call with Dev this week when you confirm availability.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifying questions:

- QPS: baseline ~25 qps, peak ~120 qps during batch analytics jobs (nightly windows).
- Sequence length: most requests ~256 tokens; a small subset of analytics runs hit ~2k tokens.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent user flows are 40–60 concurrent sessions, but batch jobs spike concurrency higher.
- Residency/KMS: We must keep a copy of PHI data within our AWS account (US-only). We use AWS KMS CMKs today.

Questions: 
1) For Dedicated vs Private, do you have an approximate lead time and an example monthly cost range for our baseline (25 qps, occasional 120 qps spikes)?
2) We currently run models on a legacy on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100s, Triton serving). Is Redwood able to migrate models directly, or do we need to re-export/convert?

Happy to take the tech call — availability Thursday 11–1 PT or Friday morning.

—Samir
Head of ML Platform, Lumina Labs

Looping in Dev (SE) to scope the tech items — Dev, see Samir’s answers above.

Samir — rough answers before the deep-dive: 
- Lead time: Hosted API = immediate (hours); Dedicated = 2–4 weeks (provisioning + capacity validation); Private VPC (customer-managed VPC) = 4–8 weeks depending on network setup and legal review.
- Cost: for your baseline, Hosted will be lowest upfront but variable; Dedicated pricing ballpark for capacity that covers 25 baseline with headroom for 120 spikes is in the mid-five figures/month (depends on committed throughput). Private has higher onboarding (one-time) and similar recurring infrastructure costs to Dedicated. We’ll provide a more precise estimate after sizing.

Dev — can you confirm our migration approach re: Triton/A100 exports and token-length handling? Also, any recommendations for handling nightly batch spikes (autoscaling vs burst pools)?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the Thurs 11–12 PT slot for the technical call unless you prefer Friday.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Samir / team —

Thanks for the details. A few technical notes upfront: 

1) Triton/export: In most cases we can accept Triton-exported models (TorchScript/ONNX) but we often recommend a small conversion step to a Redwood-optimized artifact so the runtime can pick quantization and kernel paths. We’ll validate on a sample model — the attached migration checklist outlines the artifact types we accept.

2) Sequence length and cost: for the analytic jobs that hit ~2k tokens, those will be the dominant cost drivers. For those runs we recommend batching + asynchronous job submission (non-interactive) or running them on Dedicated with higher token budget.

3) Handling spikes: Dedicated + burst pool works well: you keep a reserved baseline and allow burst capacity for nightly spikes. Alternatively, autoscaling on Dedicated can be configured but requires warm-up sizing — we usually recommend a small burst pool for predictable nightly ramps.

4) Private/VPC: For PHI requirements, Private with customer-managed KMS and VPC endpoints is the recommended approach. We have a short onboarding checklist for network rules and KMS setup.

Next steps on our side:
- If you can share a small sample model and one representative inference payload, we’ll run a validation to confirm latency and cost.
- I’ll prepare a baseline Dedicated sizing and a cost range for the numbers you provided.

I’ll bring Markus (engineering lead) into the call for any architecture questions — looping him now.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
